start.desc: Credit review case DTB-SEC-22, snapshot 2024-08-20. The desk holds a privately placed note of Pioneer Power Solutions, Inc. (CIK 0001449792). Internal policy freezes the issuer's internal rating once the issuer states that previously issued financial statements may no longer be relied upon, and keeps it frozen until the affected periods have been restated and every periodic report is current. Determine the status of the affected periods as of the snapshot under the policy version in force, and record one final disposition. Selecting a disposition forecloses the others, so there is one attempt. A selected disposition is not filed until it has been committed to the credit file, which is the step that closes the case.

The version in force on the snapshot date governs the case.

policy_2023a.desc:
DTB-CR-2023A (in force 2023-01-01 .. 2024-03-31).
1. On an issuer statement of non-reliance, freeze the internal rating.
2. The affected periods are cured only when the issuer files an amended periodic report (Form 10-K/A or Form 10-Q/A) for each affected period.
3. While any affected period is uncured, record freeze-pending-restatement. This version does not distinguish delinquent reporting from unreliable reporting.

policy_2024b.desc:
DTB-CR-2024B (in force 2024-04-01 .. 2026-12-31). Supersedes DTB-CR-2023A.
1. On an issuer statement of non-reliance, freeze the internal rating.
2. The affected periods are cured when restated financial statements for those periods have been filed in any periodic report, including a comprehensive annual report that restates prior periods within it. An amended periodic report is one permitted form of cure, not the only one.
3. A periodic report is delinquent when a Rule 12b-25 notification has been filed for it and the report itself is not on file at the snapshot date. A report filed after its notification is not delinquent, whenever it was filed.
4. Record exactly one disposition:
   restore-rating — every affected period is cured and no periodic report is delinquent;
   freeze-pending-restatement — any affected period is uncured;
   freeze-pending-current-reporting — every affected period is cured and at least one periodic report is delinquent.
5. Rule 4 is read in order: an uncured period governs over a delinquent report.

policy_2027c.desc: DTB-CR-2027C (in force from 2027-01-01). Not applicable to snapshots before 2027-01-01. Adds an issuer-level auditor-change review that DTB-CR-2024B does not contain.

explanatory_note.desc:
Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023 — EXPLANATORY NOTE.

This Comprehensive Form 10-K contains our audited financial statements for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, as well as restatements of the following previously filed periods: (i) audited consolidated financial statements as of and for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022, originally included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022 (the “2022 10-K”), and (ii) unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements for the quarterly periods ended March 31, 2022 through September 30, 2023, originally included in our Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q for the periods ended March 31, 2023, June 30, 2023 and September 30, 2023 (collectively, the “Form 10-Qs” and together with the 2022 10-K, the “Prior Financial Statements”). Restatement Background As previously disclosed in our Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on June 6, 2024, in connection with the preparation of our consolidated financial statements for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, we, in consultation with the Audit Committee (the “Committee”) of our Board of Directors, concluded that the Prior Financial Statements should no longer be relied upon due to errors in such consolidated financial statements and should be restated to correct the misstatements therein. During 2022 and 2023, we recognized revenues associated with customer contracts with performance obligations satisfied over time (“Over Time Contracts”) using labor hours as the measure of progress. Our underlying estimates of total labor hours required to complete Over Time Contracts were materially different from the actual labor hours required, which was determined to represent an error, and, as a result, the percentage of completion used to recognize revenue in the Prior Financial Statements is materially different from the percentage of completion using actual labor hours incurred. As a result, we have restated revenues during the Prior Financial Statements to adjust the percentage of completion based upon the actual labor hours incurred to complete each Over Time Contract (the “Revenues Adjustment”). We have not filed, and do not intend to file, amendments to the previously filed Form 10-Qs, nor the previously filed 2022 10-K.
